description: The mount point path (e.g. a drive letter root or mount folder) assigned to a volume when it is mounted.
hunting_notes: Pairs with VolumeDriveLetter/VolumeName/VolumeRealDeviceName to fully describe a mount event; useful for spotting new/unexpected mount points, especially for removable media.

join_candidates.why: both describe how the same mounted volume is addressed on the filesystem

evidence: type=keyword, 4 volume-mount events (FsVolumeMounted, FsVolumeUnmounted, MountedVolume, RemovableMediaVolumeMounted), always co-occurring with VolumeDriveLetter/VolumeName/VolumeRealDeviceName — standard Windows storage-stack vocabulary.

description: The underlying physical/virtual device path backing a mounted volume (distinct from VolumeFileSystemDevice, which appears to name the filesystem device object/class rather than the specific device instance).
hunting_notes: Use alongside VolumeFileSystemDevice/VolumeFileSystemDriver to fully resolve what physical or virtual medium a drive letter actually points to.

join_candidates.why: both name device-level aspects of the same mounted volume and co-occur on all volume-mount events

evidence: type=keyword, 4 events (FsVolumeMounted, MountedVolume, RemovableMediaVolumeMounted, SnapshotVolumeMounted), always co-occurring with VolumeFileSystemDevice/Driver and VolumeMountPoint. Exact distinction from VolumeFileSystemDevice is a reasonable but unconfirmed reading of the two names.

description: A retry/attempt counter for an operation such as a large-file upload, incremented each time the operation is retried.
hunting_notes: A high AttemptNumber on LfoUploadStart/DataComplete may indicate network instability or an upload being actively blocked/interfered with.

join_candidates.why: AttemptNumber counts retries of the specific upload identified by UploadId

evidence: type=long, 3 events (EtwComponentResponse, LfoUploadDataComplete, LfoUploadStart), the latter two co-occurring with UploadId/LfoUploadFlags — 'attempt number' is an unambiguous name for a retry counter.

description: The name of the Windows authentication package used for a logon (e.g. NTLM, Kerberos, Negotiate).
hunting_notes: Classic Windows logon-analysis field — NTLM logons where Kerberos would be expected, or unusual packages, are a common lateral-movement/pass-the-hash signal.

join_candidates.why: together they fully characterize how a logon (UserLogon/UserLogoff/UserIdentity) was authenticated

evidence: type=keyword, 3 events (UserIdentity, UserLogoff, UserLogon), always co-occurring with LogonType/LogonDomain/UserSid — standard Windows Security-event terminology (matches auditing concept 'Authentication Package' in Windows Event ID 4624/4625).

description: The code-signing certificate details (e.g. subject, issuer) extracted from a module/file involved in an unsigned-module or sensitive-handle detection.
hunting_notes: Inspect alongside ExtendedKeyUsages/PublicKeys/SignInfoFlags to assess whether a module's signing chain is legitimate.

join_candidates.why: attribute of the same certificate captured on the same events

evidence: type blank in fields.json (consistent with a nested object), 3 events (LsassHandleFromUnsignedModule, PrivilegedProcessHandleFromUnsignedModule, SAMHashDumpFromUnsignedModule), always co-occurring with ExtendedKeyUsages/PublicKeys/SignInfoFlags/FileSigningTime — standard PKI field cluster.

description: Part of the sensor's three-part configuration identifier (ConfigIDBase/ConfigIDBuild/ConfigIDPlatform) reported at agent connect/online time, identifying the applied sensor policy/config revision.
hunting_notes: Useful to detect hosts running an outdated or divergent sensor configuration across a fleet.

join_candidates.why: sibling components of the same sensor configuration identifier, always reported together

evidence: type=keyword, 3 events (AgentConnect, AgentOnline, SensorHeartbeat), always co-occurring with ConfigIDBuild, ConfigIDPlatform, ConfigurationVersion, ProvisionState — clearly one part of a related config-identity tuple, though the exact semantic split between Base/Build/Platform is not documented on disk.

description: The SHA256 hash of scanned or egressed content (e.g. a script's body, or data leaving the host via DataEgress) — distinct from the hash of the process image itself.
hunting_notes: Use to fingerprint script/data content independent of file name, for correlating the same malicious script snippet across hosts.

join_candidates.why: same hash algorithm and value space, just scoped to scanned/egressed content rather than an executable image

evidence: type=keyword, 3 events (DataEgress, ScriptControlScanInfo, ScriptControlScanTelemetry), name is unambiguous (SHA256 + HashData naming convention used throughout this schema for hash fields).

description: The manufacturer name of a connected accessory/USB device.
hunting_notes: Useful for peripheral/USB device inventory and spotting unusual or spoofed manufacturer strings on connected devices.

join_candidates.why: sibling descriptive attribute of the same connected device

evidence: type=keyword, 3 events (AccessoryConnected, DcUsbDeviceConnected, DcUsbDeviceDisconnected), always co-occurring with DeviceProduct/DeviceInstanceId — standard USB device descriptor terminology.

description: The product name of a connected accessory/USB device.
hunting_notes: Same use as DeviceManufacturer — peripheral inventory and anomaly spotting.

join_candidates.why: sibling descriptive attribute of the same connected device

evidence: type=keyword, same 3 events as DeviceManufacturer, always co-occurring with it.

description: The full command line of the grandparent process (the parent of the process's parent) in the process ancestry chain.
hunting_notes: Extends process-lineage visibility two levels up — useful for identifying the ultimate legitimate-looking launcher (e.g. explorer.exe, a script host) behind a chain of suspicious child processes.

join_candidates.why: same ancestry chain, one level closer to the event's process
numeric identity of the same grandparent process this field's command line belongs to

evidence: 3 events (Event_DetectionSummaryEvent, FalconProcessHandleOpDetectInfo, ScriptControlScanTelemetry), always co-occurring with ParentCommandLine/GrandparentImageFileName — consistent process-ancestry naming used throughout the schema.

description: A field on sensitive-handle-open detection events (LsassHandleFromUnsignedModule, PrivilegedProcessHandleFromUnsignedModule, SuspiciousPrivilegedProcessHandle) whose name suggests it indicates whether the requested handle was actually created/granted rather than blocked.
hunting_notes: If it does mark success/failure of the handle-open, it lets a hunter separate detections where the sensitive access actually succeeded from ones where it was blocked/failed — a materially different severity.

join_candidates.why: describes the outcome of the same handle-open request whose requested rights DesiredAccess captures

evidence: type=keyword, 3 events, always co-occurring with DesiredAccess/Status/TargetProcessId. No decode table or CIM mapping found to confirm the exact value semantics.

description: A container/object field grouping MITRE ATT&CK metadata (MitreAttack.Tactic, .TacticID, .Technique, .TechniqueID, .PatternID) on cloud-generated lead/detection-summary events.
hunting_notes: Reference the child fields directly (MitreAttack.Tactic etc.) in tools that don't flatten nested objects.
evidence: type blank (nested/object), 3 events (Event_AutomatedLeadSummaryEvent, Event_DataProtectionDetectionSummaryEvent, Event_EppDetectionSummaryEvent), and its own co-occurrence set is exactly its five MitreAttack.* children, confirming a parent/child nested relationship.

description: The MITRE ATT&CK tactic name for a cloud-generated lead/detection-summary event, sibling to MitreAttack.TacticID (the tactic's ID code).
hunting_notes: Same ATT&CK vocabulary as Tactic/Attacks.Tactic elsewhere in the schema; normalize the three spellings for unified ATT&CK coverage reporting.

join_candidates.why: name/ID pair for the same tactic on the same event
same ATT&CK tactic vocabulary used on a different (non-lead) detection-summary event family

evidence: 3 events, always co-occurring with MitreAttack.TacticID/Technique/TechniqueID; name is the standard MITRE ATT&CK term and parallels Tactic/Attacks.Tactic elsewhere in this schema.

description: The MITRE ATT&CK tactic ID code (e.g. TA0005) for a cloud-generated lead/detection-summary event, sibling to MitreAttack.Tactic (the tactic's display name).
data_format: UTF-8 string (ATT&CK tactic ID, e.g. TA00xx)
hunting_notes: Machine-stable identifier for ATT&CK tactic mapping/dashboards, preferable to the display name for joins across data sources.

join_candidates.why: ID/name pair for the same tactic on the same event

evidence: Same 3 events as MitreAttack.Tactic, always co-occurring with it; 'TacticID' naming convention (paired ID/name fields) is used consistently for Technique/TechniqueID as well.

description: The MITRE ATT&CK technique name for a cloud-generated lead/detection-summary event, sibling to MitreAttack.TechniqueID.
hunting_notes: Same ATT&CK vocabulary as Technique/Attacks.Technique elsewhere in the schema.

join_candidates.why: name/ID pair for the same technique on the same event
same ATT&CK technique vocabulary used on a different detection-summary event family

evidence: 3 events, always co-occurring with MitreAttack.Tactic/TacticID/TechniqueID; standard MITRE ATT&CK naming.

description: The MITRE ATT&CK technique ID code (e.g. T1055) for a cloud-generated lead/detection-summary event, sibling to MitreAttack.Technique.
data_format: UTF-8 string (ATT&CK technique ID, e.g. T1xxx)
hunting_notes: Machine-stable identifier preferable to the display name for cross-source ATT&CK joins.

join_candidates.why: ID/name pair for the same technique on the same event

evidence: Same 3 events as the other MitreAttack.* fields, always co-occurring with them.

description: A generic display-name field on cloud-generated lead/detection-summary events (Event_AutomatedLeadSummaryEvent, Event_DataProtectionDetectionSummaryEvent, Event_EppDetectionSummaryEvent); likely the name of the lead, policy, or indicator the record represents, but the exact referent differs by event type.
hunting_notes: Check event_simpleName before treating 'Name' as a single consistent concept — it labels different things (a lead vs. a DLP policy/indicator vs. a detection) depending on which of the three events it appears on.
evidence: type=keyword, 3 events, each a different cloud detection/lead-summary type with different sibling fields (LeadId/LeadType vs. Policy.Name/AnodeIndicators.Name vs. detection-specific fields) — the generic name and heterogeneous context prevent a single confident definition.

description: The macOS Open Directory attribute name (e.g. a dsAttrType) being added, removed, or set on a directory-service record.
hunting_notes: Pairs with ODRecordName/ODRecordType/ODNodeName to fully describe a directory-service attribute change — useful for macOS local-account tampering hunts.

join_candidates.why: the attribute named here belongs to the OD record identified by ODRecordName

evidence: type=keyword, 3 events, all OpenDirectoryAttribute{Add,Remove,Set} — unambiguous macOS Open Directory terminology.

description: The macOS Open Directory record name (e.g. a username or group name) that a directory-service attribute operation targeted.
hunting_notes: Identifies which account/group was affected by an OpenDirectoryAttribute* change.

join_candidates.why: sibling field describing which attribute of this record changed

evidence: Same 3 OpenDirectoryAttribute* events as ODAttributeName, always co-occurring with it and ODRecordType/ODNodeName.

description: A list of detection pattern/signature IDs that matched, complementing the singular PatternId field on the same handle-access and logon-behavior detection events.
hunting_notes: Use when a single event can be flagged by multiple overlapping detection patterns — PatternId alone may only show one of several matches.

join_candidates.why: PatternIdList is the plural/list form of the same detection-pattern identifier concept

evidence: type=match_only_text, 3 events (FalconProcessHandleOpDetectInfo, LogonBehaviorCompositionDetectInfo, XumdHookEvent), always co-occurring with the singular PatternId and with ParentProcessPatternIdList/GrandparentProcessPatternIdList variants on the first event.

description: The identifier of the policy or rule that matched, used generically across different policy engines (DLP in DataEgress, file-integrity rules in FileIntegrityMonitorRuleMatched — though that event uses PolicyRuleID/PolicyRuleGroupID instead, and firewall rules).
hunting_notes: Use to pivot from a triggered event back to the specific policy/rule configuration responsible, for tuning noisy rules.
evidence: type=keyword, 3 events (DataEgress, FileIntegrityMonitorRuleMatched, FirewallRuleIP4Matched) spanning three different policy subsystems (DLP, FIM, firewall) — the name is generic and reused across unrelated policy engines, so treat the exact ID namespace as engine-specific.

description: A field on module-load/classification events (ClassifiedModuleLoad, ImageHash, MachOHeaderParsed) whose name suggests it flags whether the module being reported is the process's main/primary executable image rather than a secondary loaded library.
hunting_notes: If confirmed as a primary-vs-secondary flag, useful to filter module-load telemetry down to main-executable loads only.
evidence: type=keyword, 3 events, co-occurring with ImageFileName/SHA256HashData/ModuleCharacteristics but with no decode table or CIM mapping to confirm the exact semantics of the name.

description: The real user ID (UID) of the process on Linux/Unix, part of the POSIX real/effective/saved credential set captured alongside RGID (real GID), SVUID/SVGID (saved), and UID.
hunting_notes: Useful for spotting privilege-escalation patterns where RUID differs from the effective/saved UID (e.g. via setuid binaries) on Linux hosts.

join_candidates.why: companion real-ID field (group) captured on the same Linux process/FIM events

evidence: type=keyword, 3 events (FileIntegrityMonitorRuleMatched, ProcessRollup2, SyntheticProcessRollup2 — all Linux-relevant), always co-occurring with RGID, SVGID, SVUID, UID, GID — the standard POSIX real/effective/saved credential field cluster.

description: The registry key name/path targeted by an operation, used on some registry events (RegGenericKeyUpdate, SAMHashDumpFromUnsignedModule, SuspiciousRegAsepUpdate) in place of or alongside RegObjectName.
hunting_notes: Same persistence/tamper hunting value as RegObjectName; check which of the two names is populated per event type.

join_candidates.why: overlapping concept (registry key path) used on a different subset of registry-related events

evidence: type=keyword, 3 events, always in registry-modification/detection contexts (RegOperationType, RegType, RegPostObjectName/RegRootObjectName present) — standard Windows registry terminology.

description: A name/identifier for the scripted content being scanned by Script Control (e.g. AMSI-style script scanning), paired with the script's SHA256 (ContentSHA256HashData) and raw content.
hunting_notes: Use with ContentSHA256HashData to correlate repeated executions of the same suspicious script snippet across hosts, even when the calling process/file differs.

join_candidates.why: co-occurs on the same script-scan events and identifies the same script content by hash

evidence: type=keyword, 3 events (ScriptControlDetectInvalidInfo, ScriptControlScanInfo, ScriptControlScanTelemetry), always co-occurring with ContentSHA256HashData/ScriptContent/OriginalContentLength.

description: A human-readable severity label (e.g. 'Low', 'High', 'Critical') for a detection, paired with a numeric Severity field on cloud detection-summary events.
hunting_notes: Preferred over the raw numeric Severity for dashboards/alert triage readability; use the numeric Severity for sorting/thresholding.

join_candidates.why: label/numeric pair for the same detection severity

evidence: type=keyword, 3 events (Event_DataProtectionDetectionSummaryEvent, Event_DetectionSummaryEvent, Event_EppDetectionSummaryEvent), all cloud detection-summary types where a paired 'Severity' numeric field is also present in the schema.

description: The name of the SMB share involved in a client or server share-access event.
hunting_notes: Useful for lateral-movement/data-exfiltration hunting on SMB — flag access to administrative shares (C$, ADMIN$) or unusual share names.

join_candidates.why: identifies the remote host accessing/hosting the same SMB share on client-side events

evidence: type=keyword, 3 events (SmbClientShareClosedEtw, SmbClientShareOpenedEtw, SmbServerShareOpenedEtw) — name is unambiguous.

description: The name of a Windows Scheduled Task that was registered, modified, or deleted.
hunting_notes: Core persistence-hunting field — new/renamed scheduled tasks with random-looking names or tasks executing from unusual paths (see TaskExecCommand) are classic persistence indicators.
evidence: type=keyword, 3 events (ScheduledTaskDeleted, ScheduledTaskModified, ScheduledTaskRegistered), co-occurring with TaskAuthor/TaskExecCommand/TaskXml on the latter two.

description: The relative identifier (RID) portion of a Windows user's SID — the final component that, combined with the domain SID, forms the user's full SID — captured on account lifecycle events.
hunting_notes: Well-known RIDs (e.g. 500 for the built-in Administrator) are useful for flagging sensitive-account activity even when the display name has been changed.

join_candidates.why: UserRid combined with DomainSid reconstructs the account's full SID

evidence: type=keyword, 3 events (UserAccountAddedToGroup, UserAccountCreated, UserAccountDeleted), co-occurring with DomainSid/GroupRid — standard Windows Security Identifier (SID) terminology.

description: The label/name assigned to a mounted volume.
hunting_notes: Useful alongside VolumeDriveLetter/VolumeMountPoint for identifying specific removable media by its assigned label across multiple mount events.

join_candidates.why: both describe the same mounted volume instance across the volume-mount event family

evidence: cim_reachable=True (mapped to file_name/file_path in CIM, likely a generic path-model reuse), 6 events (FsVolumeMounted, FsVolumeUnmounted, MountedVolume, RemovableMediaVolumeMounted, SnapshotVolumeMounted, VolumeSnapshotDeleted) — all volume lifecycle events.

description: The Windows file attribute bitmask (e.g. FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY, HIDDEN, SYSTEM, ARCHIVE) of a file at create/open time.
hunting_notes: Flag combinations like HIDDEN+SYSTEM on a newly-written executable are a classic evasion indicator; CrowdStrike's own TA provides a decode lookup (FileAttributes_meaning) for this bitmask.
evidence: cim_reachable=True via a LOOKUP-type CIM mapping ('FileAttributes_meaning'), confirming it is a decodable Windows file-attributes bitmask; appears on 5 filesystem minifilter events (DirectoryCreate, FsPostOpenSnapshotFile, NewExecutableWritten, NewScriptWritten, RansomwareOpenFile).

description: The string representation of a registry value's data, when a registry value is created or modified.
hunting_notes: Primary field for inspecting the actual content written into an autostart/persistence registry value (e.g. a Run-key command line).

join_candidates.why: RegStringValue is the data written into the value named by RegValueName

evidence: cim_reachable=True (mapped to registry_value_data), type=match_only_text, 5 registry-update events, always co-occurring with RegValueName/RegType/RegObjectName.

description: The socket/network address family (e.g. AF_INET, AF_INET6, AF_UNIX) of a created socket or network interface.
hunting_notes: Useful to distinguish IPv4/IPv6/Unix-domain socket activity when hunting on CreateSocket telemetry.
evidence: type=keyword, 2 events (CreateSocket, LocalIpAddressIP6), co-occurring with SocketType/NetlinkFamily on CreateSocket — 'address family' is standard, unambiguous BSD-sockets terminology.

description: An index into CrowdStrike's internal ASEP (Auto-Start Extensibility Point) classification table for a registry-based autostart entry, paired with AsepClass/AsepFlags/AsepValueType.
hunting_notes: Can be used to filter autostart telemetry to specific ASEP categories without string-matching registry paths, but the index-to-category mapping isn't present in this KB.

join_candidates.why: the ASEP classification applies to the registry autostart entry named by RegObjectName on the same event

evidence: type=keyword, 2 events (AsepKeyUpdate, AsepValueUpdate), always co-occurring with AsepClass/AsepFlags/AsepValueType — clearly part of CrowdStrike's ASEP (autostart) classification field family, though no decode table confirms specific index values.

description: A file path/name associated with a cloud detection (e.g. the malicious file that triggered the detection), on detection-summary events.
hunting_notes: Complements FileName/FilePath on the same detection-summary events for identifying the artifact behind a detection.

join_candidates.why: likely names the same or a related artifact captured elsewhere on the same detection event

evidence: type=keyword, 2 events (Event_DetectionSummaryEvent, Event_EppDetectionSummaryEvent), co-occurring with FileName/FilePath/MD5String/SHA1String/SHA256String — clearly part of the file-identification field cluster on these detection events, though its precise relationship to FileName/FilePath isn't spelled out.

description: The string-encoded form of AuthenticationUuid — a Windows logon-session UUID — captured on group/user identity events.
hunting_notes: Use as a stable, human-readable join key for a logon session when the binary AuthenticationUuid form isn't convenient to work with.

join_candidates.why: string-encoded form of the same UUID value
both identify the same logon session via different ID schemes

evidence: type=keyword, 2 events (GroupIdentity, UserIdentity), always co-occurring with the raw AuthenticationUuid field — name directly states it's the string form of that UUID.

description: The SHA256 hash of a driver/module's Authenticode signature blob, distinct from SHA256HashData (the hash of the file's own content).
hunting_notes: Useful for clustering files signed by the same certificate/signature blob even when file content (and thus SHA256HashData) differs.

join_candidates.why: parallel hash field on the same events, but over the signature rather than the file content

evidence: type=keyword, 2 events (DriverLoad, ModuleCertificateInfo2), co-occurring with SHA256HashData, CertificateIssuer/Publisher, AuthenticodeHashData (non-SHA256 variant) — the naming convention (Authenticode + HashData + SHA256) makes the signature-hash reading likely, though not independently confirmed.

description: The Azure region/location of a cloud resource (e.g. a public IP or virtual machine) discovered via cloud-asset inventory.
hunting_notes: Useful for geo-scoping cloud asset inventory and spotting resources unexpectedly provisioned in an unfamiliar region.

join_candidates.why: both are location/organizational metadata for the same Azure resource

evidence: type=keyword, 2 events (AzurePublicIpAddress, AzureVirtualMachine), co-occurring with AzureResourceGroup/AzureSubscriptionId/AzureVMName — standard Azure Resource Manager metadata terminology.

description: The Azure resource group containing a cloud resource (public IP or virtual machine) discovered via cloud-asset inventory.
hunting_notes: Standard Azure organizational unit for scoping/ownership — useful for attributing cloud assets to a team or environment.

join_candidates.why: both are organizational/location metadata for the same Azure resource

evidence: Same 2 events as AzureLocation, always co-occurring with it and AzureSubscriptionId — standard Azure Resource Manager term.

description: The sequence number of this record within a batched/paginated inventory report (e.g. installed browser extensions, mounted volumes), paired with BatchDataTotal.
hunting_notes: Use with BatchDataTotal to detect truncated or incomplete batch reports before drawing conclusions from partial inventory data.

join_candidates.why: together they describe this record's position within a total batch size

evidence: type=keyword, 2 events (InstalledBrowserExtension, MountedVolume), always co-occurring with BatchDataTotal and BatchTimestamp — clear batch/pagination naming convention.

description: The total number of records in a batched/paginated inventory report, paired with BatchDataNumber.
hunting_notes: Same use as BatchDataNumber — verify report completeness.

join_candidates.why: together they describe this record's position within a total batch size

evidence: Same 2 events as BatchDataNumber, always co-occurring with it.

description: The timestamp at which a batched inventory report (e.g. browser extensions, mounted volumes) was generated.
hunting_notes: Use to determine the freshness of batch-collected inventory data relative to the event's own timestamp.
evidence: type=date, 2 events (InstalledBrowserExtension, MountedVolume), always co-occurring with BatchDataNumber/BatchDataTotal — name and type are unambiguous.

description: The BIOS manufacturer string of the host, part of hardware inventory reported at agent-online time and in TPM PCR events.
hunting_notes: Standard hardware/asset-inventory field; useful for fleet hardware profiling and detecting VM/sandbox environments (e.g. common virtualization BIOS vendors).

join_candidates.why: sibling BIOS inventory attribute captured on the same events

evidence: type=keyword, 2 events (AgentOnline, TcgPcrInfo), co-occurring with BiosVersion/BiosReleaseDate/SystemManufacturer — standard hardware inventory terminology.

description: The BIOS release date of the host, part of hardware inventory.
hunting_notes: Very old BIOS release dates can indicate unpatched firmware, relevant to firmware-level threat hunting alongside TcgPcrInfo's PCR values.

join_candidates.why: sibling BIOS inventory attribute

evidence: type=date, same 2 events as BiosManufacturer, always co-occurring with it and BiosVersion.

description: The Linux process's permitted capabilities set (cap_prm) — the POSIX capabilities the process is allowed to use, whether or not currently effective.
hunting_notes: Useful for Linux privilege-escalation hunting — processes with unexpected capabilities like CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_SETUID in their permitted set warrant review.

join_candidates.why: both are part of the same Linux process credential/capability record on ProcessRollup2/SyntheticProcessRollup2

evidence: type=keyword, 2 events (ProcessRollup2, SyntheticProcessRollup2), co-occurring with GID/RUID/RGID/SVUID/SVGID — the Linux POSIX credential field cluster; 'CapPrm' directly matches the Linux kernel's 'cap_prm' terminology.

description: The CompanyName string from a PE file's version-info resource (e.g. driver or executable metadata).
hunting_notes: Useful for spotting spoofed or missing company names on drivers/executables masquerading as legitimate software.

join_candidates.why: sibling PE version-info attribute captured on the same events

evidence: type=keyword, 2 events (DriverLoad, PeVersionInfo), co-occurring with FileVersion/OriginalFilename/FixedFileVersion — standard PE VERSIONINFO resource fields.

description: A generic supplementary-context payload whose content differs by event (e.g. exclusion context on DetectionExcluded, unclear content on EndOfProcess); no single schema is confirmed from this KB.
evidence: type blank in fields.json, only 2 events (DetectionExcluded, EndOfProcess) with otherwise unrelated field sets (ExclusionType/ExclusionSource vs. a large stats/counter block) — the generic name and heterogeneous context prevent a confident single definition.

description: A bitmask of supported CPU instruction-set features/extensions on the host, part of hardware inventory.
hunting_notes: Primarily an asset-inventory field; occasionally useful to confirm hardware capability (e.g. for sensor feature gating) rather than for direct threat hunting.

join_candidates.why: sibling CPU inventory attribute captured on the same events

evidence: type=keyword, 2 events (AgentOnline, SystemCapacity), co-occurring with CpuSignature/CpuVendor — clearly a CPU-feature bitmask by name and context, though no decode table confirms individual bit meanings.

description: The CPU signature/model identifier (akin to the x86 CPUID signature) of the host, part of hardware inventory.
hunting_notes: Asset-inventory/fleet-profiling field rather than a direct hunting signal.

join_candidates.why: sibling CPU inventory attribute

evidence: Same 2 events as CpuFeaturesMask, always co-occurring with it and CpuVendor.

description: A human-readable description of a cloud detection (Event_DataProtectionDetectionSummaryEvent, Event_EppDetectionSummaryEvent).
hunting_notes: Useful for analyst-facing detection summaries/alert text, not typically a good machine-hunting pivot field itself.
evidence: type=keyword, 2 events, both cloud detection-summary types; generic but unambiguous in this narrow context.
